description: We are a small, hands-on team that likes to ship working things in a weekend. Our background is software and machine learning: simulations, maps, data pipelines and polished demos. We want to turn NASA data into something a real person can use on a bad day. We're looking for a designer or storyteller, a data/Earth-science person and anyone who enjoys building.
summary:
Keep an eye on the places you love. From orbit.

Last summer, a factory building in our home town, Stalowa Wola in Poland, grew 4-5 millimetres in the heat. Nobody noticed. A satellite did.

NISAR, the new NASA and ISRO radar satellite, sees almost every place on land about every 12 days, through clouds and at night, and its data is free. But every pass arrives as gigabytes of radar echoes made for specialists.

Watchover turns them into plain words. You follow the places you love, and it tells you when one of them changes and why: the spot before and after, how sure we are and the exact NISAR pass behind it. For owners and insurers it shows which buildings move with heat, each one checked against patches of open ground.

We built it on real NISAR data: 53 passes over Stalowa Wola since October 2025, 33 patches of forest gone (101 hectares), a frozen forest told apart from a felled one, plus Mexico City and three world events: the Hayli Gubbi eruption, the La Guaira earthquake and the Chokwe flood.

The cosmos is closer than London: space begins about 100 km up, NISAR flies at 747 km, and London is 1,550 km from Stalowa Wola.
details:
LINKS
Live app: https://watchover.pl
Code: https://github.com/TiVoP1/watchover-app

THE PROBLEM
NISAR, the NASA and ISRO radar satellite launched in 2025, images almost all of Earth's land about every 12 days, through clouds and at night, for free. But each pass is a 2 to 13 GB file that only specialists can read, so almost nobody hears what it sees.

WHAT WATCHOVER DOES
- Follow the places you love, and Watchover tells you when one of them changes and why: forest gone, fields changed, the forest froze, ground reworked. Each report shows the spot before and after, how sure we are and the exact NISAR pass.
- Play the year: 26 seconds through a place's radar year, stopping at each clear change.
- For owners and insurers: millimetre motion of buildings, checked against patches of open ground. A building that moves unlike most is marked "Worth watching": a candidate for a closer look, never an alarm.
- Five places today: Stalowa Wola, Mexico City and three world events.

WHAT WE FOUND ON REAL NISAR DATA
- Stalowa Wola, Poland: 53 passes since October 2025. On 30 of those days at least half of the view was cloud (estimate); the radar saw the ground every time.
- 33 patches of forest gone (101 hectares) and 29 felling strips, all 28 strips with a clear view confirmed by NASA HLS optical images. With NASA GEDI lidar: about 29,500 tonnes of stored CO2 lost (estimate).
- On Christmas morning 2025 the forest went dark on radar while the town did not: frost, not felling.
- A factory building moves 4 to 5 mm towards the satellite on warm evenings (NASA POWER temperatures, an estimate). None of 3,180 positions on stable open ground followed the heat as clearly.
- Mexico City: ground moving 19 cm away from the satellite in 348 days. Hayli Gubbi, Ethiopia: a new dark stain of about 8 km² after the eruption. La Guaira, Venezuela: the coast about 50-80 cm west relative to central Caracas after the earthquake (estimate). Chokwe, Mozambique: about 150 km² of new open water (estimate).

HOW IT WORKS
A Python pipeline reads only about 13 MB of each NISAR product: GCOV backscatter for changes, with a frost guard; GSLC for coherence and building motion against rings of nearby ground; GUNW for ground motion. Every threshold and source scene is written into the outputs, and estimates carry a label.

WHY IT MATTERS
People learn too late that the forest behind their parents' house is gone or that a building is moving. Watchover makes a free radar readable in seconds for families abroad, forest owners and insurers, showing land, never people.

BUSINESS
Free for three places; paid plans add places, alerts and family sharing. Insurers, property and forest owners and carbon verifiers get an API with change events, structure motion and carbon estimates. No government money.

TOOLS
Python (numpy, h5py, fsspec), TypeScript, React, MapLibre GL, Vite, Tailwind CSS, ffmpeg; NASA Earthdata Login, ASF search API.
